ranked.headline: Models fuse multi-omics, imaging and clinical inputs for prediction and subtyping
ranked.summary: Heterogeneous omics, pathology and clinical data are increasingly combined in graph, neural and factorization models for prediction and subtyping.

ranked.headline: Learned and physics-based models predict protein binding affinity, sites and partners
ranked.summary: Sequence-plus-structure graph and language-model architectures are now applied to partner-specific prediction, alongside benchmarks exposing scorer bias.

ranked.headline: Computational methods map cell identity and spatial structure across omics and imaging
ranked.summary: Benchmarks of LLM and traditional annotation tools now test reference and method choice across scRNA-seq datasets, shaping cross-dataset inference.

ranked.headline: Protein language model embeddings combined with structure for function prediction
ranked.summary: Pretrained protein language model embeddings recur as inputs across function, interaction, structure, and allergenicity prediction in recent publications.

ranked.headline: Temporal ordering of spatial transcriptomic microenvironments and cell fate trajectories
ranked.summary: Sequential spatial slides and multi-timepoint single-cell data now support explicit modeling of temporal ordering in tissue and cell-fate inference.

ranked.headline: Pretrained and attention-based networks predict RNA, DNA and protein functional sites
ranked.summary: Nine studies from November 2025 apply pretrained language-model embeddings and attention to RNA, DNA and protein prediction tasks.

ranked.headline: Computational methods address noise and bias in sequencing-based genomic profiling
ranked.summary: Nanopore and single-cell sequencing data remain sparse and error-prone, driving new benchmarks and tools for variant, modification and enhancer inference.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks and packaged pipelines reshape plasmid, phage, and virome sequence analysis
ranked.summary: Recent benchmarks and open workflows show that tool performance for plasmid, phage-host, and virome analysis is context-dependent.

ranked.headline: Chromosome-scale assemblies and new tools for genome-wide inference
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications pair chromosome-level genome assemblies with alignment-free and phylogenetic analysis software.

ranked.headline: Multimodal deep learning and benchmarking reshape computational drug prediction
ranked.summary: Interpretable multimodal models now link early assays, chemical structure and clinical records to developability, toxicity and repurposing outcomes.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks and tools refine variant calling, CNV inference, and splicing analysis
ranked.summary: Pangenome graphs, T2T-CHM13 reference gains, and WGS pipeline benchmarks are reshaping how sequencing-derived variation is called and interpreted.

ranked.headline: New software spans genomic tokenization, LLM metadata curation, and variant analysis
ranked.summary: Recent releases pair LLM-based SRA metadata extraction with scalable genomic interval tokenization and structural variant tooling.

ranked.headline: Deep learning models predict methylation, TF binding, and variant effects from sequence
ranked.summary: Transformer and language-model architectures are now applied to methylation, TF binding, mosaic variant calling, and expression prediction from sequence.

ranked.headline: Evaluating how well predictors recover RNA-containing biomolecular structures
ranked.summary: CASP16 and AlphaFold3 benchmarks now test RNA-containing predictions against experimental density and diverse datasets.

ranked.headline: Deep learning models interpret noncoding and missense variant effects across genomes
ranked.summary: Interpretable genomic models now expose k-mer and position-level drivers and are benchmarked on clinical and regulatory variant effect tasks.

ranked.headline: Uncertainty-aware and multimodal classifiers for omics and pathology data
ranked.summary: Recent methods pair fusion architectures and uncertainty estimation with omics and pathology inputs to address reliability, missing data and small samples.

ranked.headline: Machine learning and simulation methods target ligand kinetics, peptides and aptamers
ranked.summary: Generative and simulation-based tools now address dissociation kinetics, multi-objective peptide optimization and aptamer selection.

ranked.headline: Open software packages integrate heterogeneous omics layers via network-level modeling
ranked.summary: Recent releases make network-based multi-omics integration available as open web servers and R packages rather than bespoke analyses.

ranked.headline: Deep learning models fuse multimodal drug data for synergy and interaction prediction
ranked.summary: Recent published work targets few-shot synergy, multimodal fusion, and splitting-based evaluation of drug synergy models.

ranked.headline: Web servers and containers package single-cell, spatial, breeding and metabolic methods
ranked.summary: Five 2025 publications deliver single-cell, spatial, breeding and metabolic methods as reproducible, accessible software tools.

ranked.headline: Faster, leaner algorithms for alignment, motif scoring, and genome size estimation
ranked.summary: Recent tools report memory reduction or over 1000-fold speedups, with ConCluD processing 89M DNA storage reads in under a minute on a 32-core server.

ranked.headline: Statistical methods refine causal gene and variant inference from association data
ranked.summary: Recent methods extend fine-mapping, GWAS follow-up validation and heterosis QTL scanning to related individuals and non-additive effects.

ranked.headline: Learned models now generate and optimize TCR, antibody, and neoantigen sequences
ranked.summary: Generative and search-based sequence models for immune recognition molecules now couple design with learned binding or immunogenicity scores.

ranked.headline: Structuring dispersed bioinformatics knowledge into linked, machine-usable resources
ranked.summary: Bioinformatics knowledge spread across publications, databases, and ontologies needs automated extraction, curation, and linkage to remain usable at scale.

ranked.headline: Statistical and kinetic inference of gene regulation from single-cell and ribosome profiling data
ranked.summary: Recent methods extend single-cell and translation datasets to cell annotation, differential testing, and kinetic parameter inference.

ranked.headline: Graph contrastive autoencoders and GCNs for spatial transcriptomics domain identification
ranked.summary: Graph encoders with contrastive objectives are now applied to spatial domain identification and gene regulatory network inference.

ranked.headline: Deep learning assigns sequencing reads and traces to discrete biological sources
ranked.summary: Learned models now assign raw nanopore current traces and metagenomic sequences to sources without fixed rules, as shown across three recent papers.

ranked.headline: Simulations Map Antibody Escape, Allosteric RNA Control, and AI-Designed Helix Stability
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply MD simulations, graph-network analysis, and AI-driven structure modeling to residue-level control in viral and designed proteins.

ranked.headline: Surface-based and connectivity models refine tau PET and cortical MRI analysis
ranked.summary: Three preprints add surface geometry, directed causal networks, and diffusion-derived connectivity to neuroimaging models of brain structure and disease.

ranked.headline: Generative and ligand-based methods advance small-molecule and covalent ligand design
ranked.summary: Recent publications pair generative design, benchmarked ligand-based screening, and covalent docking reviews for ligand discovery.
